$comment: Immutable prior-release lock artifacts. See README.md. Every field is checked by TestPriorReleaseFixturesAreImmutable; digests are SHA-256 of the file bytes.

fixtures.why: The oldest recoverable v1 shape: one extension pinned by a SINGLE scalar `integrity`, before per-platform `integrities` existed. It is the only fixture that proves the migration keeps a scalar-only entry's sole verification datum instead of dropping it with the legacy field.

The v1 shape at the release that introduced the CLI pin (LockFile.CLI). The extension entry carries BOTH the legacy scalar `integrity` and a one-platform `integrities` map, which is the pair the v2 canonical projection must resolve: map wins, scalar is dropped.

The first lock this repository ever committed at v2 — the require-v3 cutover that made v2 the read floor. Its extension entry records NO taskContract, which is the state `putnami migrate vnext` reports as drift rather than guessing at.

A fully populated v2: `taskContract: 3` recorded plus two real per-platform archive digests. It is the fixture that proves a v2→v4 migration carries every platform's digest, not just the one the migrating machine runs.

The first v3 lock: it adds the `toolchains` dimension with six per-platform Go release digests. Six digests in one entry is what makes a lossy migration visible — a projection that rebuilt the map from the running platform would drop five of them.

gaps.reason: v4 shipped in a later release but this workspace's committed lock is still v3, so no v4 artifact exists to recover. v4 is covered as the OUTPUT of MigrateLockFileToCurrent, which is the only way a v4 lock is produced from an older one.

No lock committed to this repository has ever pinned the CLI (`putnami pin` writes one, but this workspace builds the CLI from source). The per-platform `cli.integrities` preservation is therefore proven against the in-package `v1Golden`, which is labelled synthetic where it is used.
